The Justice Department may, at their discretion, conduct an inspection of any other department. This inspection should not be conducted when doing so would, in the opinion of either that department’s command-level officer or in the opinion of the Commanding Officer, impose an undue burden upon or interfere with the necessary functions of the department in question.
In the event that a command member, including the CO, blocks an inspection, the Chief Justice may overrule that officer if, in the Chief Justice’s opinion, there is a likelihood that an inspection will find serious malfeasance or incompetence that places the function of the station in jeopardy. If the Chief Justice does so, they must immediately inform CentComm via fax with a stamped and signed note. This power should not be used lightly, nor should it be used when there is a clear and present danger to the station (e.g., a union riot or a gas leak).
Inspections may be conducted by one or more members of the Justice Department, and should assess: -The structural integrity of the department -Whether dangerous equipment or elements have appropriately marked perimeters and/or are shielded from casual contact. -Whether the absence of the above or any other necessary infrastructure constitutes an unnecessary risk to crew health and safety. -Presence or absence of applicable safety and personal protective equipment, including fire safety and oxygen/nitrogen lockers, which should be fully stocked. -Status of air and fire alarms (Atmospherics should be notified prior to any tests of this equipment). -Adherence to sanitation and appearance standards. -Clear emergency pathways -Storage of controlled items, and whether they are reasonably secure or not. -Criminal violations of Standard Operating Procedure
